A 3-layer residual body of width 48 adds global context to every cell, and the recipe gives more updates (r≈1.25, ~136k steps). This should match landing layer to target layer better. import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 48
HID = 24
RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3, "gamma": 0.97, "gae_lambda": 0.95, "ent_coef": 0.005}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        W = WIDTH
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.glob_in = nn.Linear(2 * W, W)
        self.glob_out = nn.Linear(W, W)
        self.fp_proj = nn.Conv2d(W, HID, 1)
        self.fp_convs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(W, HID, (dy, dx)) for dy, dx in self.footprints])
        self.fp_out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        for m in self.fp_out:
            nn.init.normal_(m.weight, std=0.01)
            nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
        self.trunk = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.done_head.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.bias)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        h = F.relu(self.stem(obs))
        h = h + F.relu(self.conv1(h))
        g = F.relu(self.glob_in(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3)), h.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)))
        h = h + self.glob_out(g)[:, :, None, None]
        h = F.relu(h + F.relu(self.conv2(h)))
        p = self.fp_proj(h)
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            a = self.fp_convs[i](hp)
            pp = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            m = F.max_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(self.fp_out[i](F.relu(a + m)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        t = self.trunk(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3)), h.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(t)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(t).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 40
N_RES = 3
RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 3, "gamma": 0.97, "gae_lambda": 0.95, "ent_coef": 0.005}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        W = WIDTH
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.convs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1) for _ in range(N_RES)])
        self.glob_in = nn.Linear(2 * W, W)
        self.glob_out = nn.Linear(W, W)
        self.head_hid = nn.Conv2d(W, 32, 1)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(32, spec.n_types, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.place_head.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.place_head.bias)
        self.trunk = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        h = F.relu(self.stem(obs))
        for i, conv in enumerate(self.convs):
            h = h + F.relu(conv(h))
            if i == 0:
                g = F.relu(self.glob_in(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3)), h.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)))

        place = self.place_head(F.relu(self.head_hid(h))).flatten(1)
        t = self.trunk(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3)), h.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(t)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(t).squeeze(1)

    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 24
HID = 16
N_IN = 12
RECIPE = {"n_envs": 128, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 8, "ppo_epochs": 2, "gamma": 0.97, "gae_lambda": 0.95, "ent_coef": 0.005}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        W = WIDTH
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(N_IN, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.col = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 1)
        self.glob_in = nn.Linear(2 * W, W)
        self.glob_out = nn.Linear(W, W)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.fp_proj = nn.Conv2d(W, HID, 1)
        self.fp_convs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(W, HID, (dy, dx)) for dy, dx in self.footprints])
        self.fp_out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 2, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        for m in self.fp_out:
            nn.init.normal_(m.weight, std=0.01)
            nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
        self.trunk = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.done_head.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.bias)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        W = WIDTH
        b = obs[:, 0:Z]
        t = obs[:, Z:2 * Z]
        mi = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z]
        ex = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]
        b_lo = F.pad(b, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))[:, :Z]
        t_lo = F.pad(t, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))[:, :Z]
        b_hi = F.pad(b, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1))[:, 1:]
        t_hi = F.pad(t, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1))[:, 1:]
        hb = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 1].expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        ht = obs[:, 4 * Z + 1:4 * Z + 2].expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        tm = obs[:, 4 * Z + 2:4 * Z + 3].expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        zc = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.stack([b, t, mi, ex, b_lo, t_lo, b_hi, t_hi, hb, ht, tm, zc], dim=2)
        x = x.reshape(B * Z, N_IN, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.stem(x))
        hv = h.view(B, Z, W, Y, X)
        c = self.col(hv.amax(1))
        hv = hv + c[:, None]
        g = F.relu(self.glob_in(torch.cat([hv.mean((1, 3, 4)), hv.amax((1, 3, 4))], dim=1)))
        hv = hv + self.glob_out(g)[:, None, :, None, None]
        h = F.relu(hv).reshape(B * Z, W, Y, X)
        h = h + F.relu(self.conv2(h))
        p = self.fp_proj(h)
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            a = self.fp_convs[i](hp)
            pp = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            m = F.max_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(self.fp_out[i](F.relu(a + m)))
        o = torch.stack(outs, dim=1).view(B, Z, len(self.footprints), 2, Y, X)
        s = o[:, :, :, 0]
        w = torch.softmax(o[:, :, :, 1], dim=1)
        place = (w * s).sum(1).flatten(1)
        hv2 = h.view(B, Z, W, Y, X)
        tr = self.trunk(torch.cat([hv2.mean((1, 3, 4)), hv2.amax((1, 3, 4))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(tr)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(tr).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.ln = nn.LayerNorm(W)
        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(W, HEADS, batch_first=True)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.head_hid = nn.Conv2d(W, 32, 1)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(32, spec.n_types, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.place_head.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.place_head.bias)
        self.trunk = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.done_head.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.bias)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, Y, 1).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, X).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([obs, ys, xs], dim=1)
        h = F.relu(self.stem(x))
        h = h + F.relu(self.conv1(h))
        tok = h.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
        n = self.ln(tok)
        a, _ = self.attn(n, n, n, need_weights=False)
        h = h + a.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, WIDTH, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(h + F.relu(self.conv2(h)))
        place = self.place_head(F.relu(self.head_hid(h))).flatten(1)
        t = self.trunk(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3)), h.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(t)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(t).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 48
HID = 24
HEADS = 4
RECIPE = {"n_envs": 256, "rollout_len": 16, "n_minibatches": 16, "ppo_epochs": 2, "gamma": 0.97, "gae_lambda": 0.95, "ent_coef": 0.005}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        W = WIDTH
        self.footprints = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels + 2, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.ln = nn.LayerNorm(W)
        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(W, HEADS, batch_first=True)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.glob_in = nn.Linear(2 * W, W)
        self.glob_out = nn.Linear(W, W)
        self.fp_proj = nn.Conv2d(W, HID, 1)
        self.fp_convs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(W, HID, (dy, dx)) for dy, dx in self.footprints])
        self.fp_out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        for m in self.fp_out:
            nn.init.normal_(m.weight, std=0.01)
            nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)
        self.trunk = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        nn.init.normal_(self.done_head.weight, std=0.01)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.bias)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        ys = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, Y, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, Y, 1).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        xs = torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, X, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype).view(1, 1, 1, X).expand(B, 1, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([obs, ys, xs], dim=1)
        h = F.relu(self.stem(x))
        h = h + F.relu(self.conv1(h))
        tok = h.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
        n = self.ln(tok)
        a, _ = self.attn(n, n, n, need_weights=False)
        h = h + a.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, WIDTH, Y, X)
        g = F.relu(self.glob_in(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3)), h.amax((2, 3))], dim=1)))
        h = h + self.glob_out(g)[:, :, None, None]
        h = F.relu(h + F.relu(self.conv2(h)))
        p = self.fp_proj(h)
        outs = []
        for i, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            af = self.fp_convs[i](hp)
            pp = F.pad(p, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            m = F.max_pool2d(pp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(self.fp_out[i](F.relu(af + m)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        t = self.trunk(torch.cat([h.mean((2, 3)), h.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(t)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(t).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1:
No trials have run yet, and scores stay hidden all search, so later rounds can only learn about crashes and check failures. Each candidate has to be a strong, robust bet in its own right.

Two things about the task matter most:
1. **Budget:** the default trains only about 32 PPO updates, so it is very short. Smaller rollout batches and fewer epochs give more updates and more samples.
2. **Structure:** placing the right brick is a local, footprint-shaped decision. The brick lands at the highest filled cell under its footprint, and that landing layer must match the target layer in every footprint cell. Choosing DONE needs a global "nothing missing" signal.

Because a network cheaper than the starting one is still charged as costing the same, a deeper, narrower network at the same cost is effectively free.

The three bets:
- **A:** a placement head shaped like each brick's footprint, with max pooling over the footprint, plus global context.
- **B:** a deeper, narrower residual network at the same cost, with global context.
- **C:** the starting architecture with only a sample-heavy recipe, as a safe hedge.
analyses.2: Scores are hidden, so round 1 only shows that all three directions train correctly within the time limit: a footprint-aware head (r1c1), a deeper residual body (r1c2) and a recipe with more samples (r1c3). The budget is tiny, about 10k episodes, so the network's built-in assumptions probably matter most. The key judgement is per placement: the landing layer is the highest build cell under the footprint, and the brick must fill missing target cells at exactly that layer. A plain 2D conv must learn this from per-layer channels with only linear first layers. In round 2 I refine r1c1 with one change each: a recipe with more samples and fewer epochs, and a per-column MLP stem that can compare heights and layers non-linearly. The third trial is a new idea: a 2D conv shared across layers, with a learned softmax over layers that should learn to pick the landing layer. Refutation can only come from the final dev ranking.
analyses.3: No scores are visible, so every trial is useful only through the real dev ranking at the end. All 6 trials trained without errors. The trials so far test three things on their own: footprint-shaped placement heads (r1c1, r2c1, r2c2), a deeper residual net with global context (r1c2), and a recipe with more samples and fewer epochs (r1c3, r2c1). The layer-shared design (r2c3) is a gamble because it has very few parameters. The footprint head is the only idea already tried with both recipes, so it has more chances to land in the top 3. With two rounds left, I'll combine ideas that each seem plausible and test one new idea. The deep residual net (r1c2) has not been tried with the sample-heavy recipe. The footprint net has not been pushed to 1 epoch, which gives the most samples. No trial yet mixes information across the whole board in one step, so I'll test cell-to-cell self-attention. I keep every candidate at r≤1.3 so the time limit is safe.
analyses.4: No scores are shown. Every trial so far trained without errors, so the only evidence is cost and step counts. Footprint-shaped placement heads (r1c1, r2c1, r3c2, r2c2) are the most-tested idea and cost little (r≈1.3). Moving from 4 to 2 PPO epochs gives 1.4 to 1.8 times as many steps. Two ideas ran without errors but are untested in combination: cell self-attention (r3c3) and a per-cell column MLP stem (r2c2). r2c2 had the fewest steps (123k) because it used 3 epochs. In this final round I combine parts that have each worked, with one main change per trial: (1) the footprint head with self-attention, (2) the column-stem net with the 2-epoch recipe, and (3) the footprint net with the 2-epoch recipe and a higher learning rate. The higher learning rate tests whether more learning per update helps at this small budget. The best three by dev score get extra seeds, so offering three different strong variants is a hedge against seed luck.
